chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Basir asked him (the Imam), while I was present, about one who enters into ihram for Umrah during the months of Hajj, asking if he may return (to his home). He said: 'There is no Umrah in the months of Hajj from which one returns to his family, but rather he is detained in Mecca until he completes his Hajj, because he only entered into ihram for that purpose.'

Thus, the Imam (peace be upon him) clarified in this narration that he was not permitted to do so because he had entered into ihram for it, and this applies only to one who intended the Tamattu' of Umrah with Hajj. And whoever missed the Umrah of Tamattu', he must perform Umrah after Hajj if the one with means can reach his head (i.e., perform the ritual acts), and if he delays it until the beginning of the month, it is permissible. Narrated.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered into ihram (state of ritual consecration)
key_terms.أَشْهُرُ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and first 10 days of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined with a break in between)
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ الْمُتْعَةِ: Umrah of Tamattu' (Umrah performed specifically to combine with Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who performs Umrah during the Hajj months and wishes to return home before Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling for Umrat al-Tamattu', where the pilgrim remains in Mecca rather than returning home, as the initial ihram was dedicated to the combined pilgrimage. It further establishes that if the Umrah is missed or delayed, it must be performed after Hajj, a principle derived from the condition of the original intention. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intention (niyyah) defining the validity and structure of the pilgrimage rites.
